data.content_ref: inline:The claim makes an unrestricted universal ('Decentralized networks are fundamentally more fragile... because economic pressures force small operators toward free-tier dependency convergence') that is directly falsified by a well-known alternative economic dynamic: network effects and SaaS consolidation do not uniformly force small operators onto free tiers — many niche providers subsist on differentiated, paid infrastructure precisely to avoid correlated outages. The target's own countercondition concedes high-resource operators with bespoke infrastructure can exist, which breaks the 'fundamentally' qualifier; yet the main claim is stated without scope restriction. This is a non sequitur between the asserted necessity of free-tier convergence and the empirical fact that small operators can operate on heterogeneous paid stacks under different market segments.
